name: Egbere
body:
EGBERE
CR 1/2

This short unkempt infant-like creature carries a woven mat tucked in its arms and keens a melancholy cry.

XP 200
NE Small fey
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., locate thief, low-light vision; Perception +3

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 13, flat-footed 11 (+2 Dex, +1 size)
hp 9 (2d6+2)
Fort +1, Ref +5, Will +1
DR 2/cold iron

OFFENSE

Speed 25 ft.
Special Attacks sorrowful wailing
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 2nd; concentration +2)

At will—ghost sound (DC 10), prestidigitation, ventriloquism (DC 11)

STATISTICS

Str 5, Dex 14, Con 12, Int 11, Wis 7, Cha 10
Base Atk +1; CMB –3; CMD 9
Feats Endurance
Skills Climb +2, Escape Artist +7, Perception +3, Sense Motive +3, Stealth +11, Swim +2
Languages Common, Sylvan (doesn’t speak)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Egbere Mat (Su)

This woven straw mat is an egbere’s most precious and only possession, apart from the ragged clothing on its back.

If a non-fey creature steals the mat, then one week after being stolen 1 gp appears within the rolled-up mat at dusk. Each week this money is left in the mat, it doubles in amount: 1 gp, 2 gp, 4 gp, 8 gp, etc. If some of the coins are removed, only the remaining coins still left in the mat are doubled. If all the money is taken from the mat, the process starts anew one week later at dusk with 1 gp. If the stolen mat changes hands, the coin creating process starts anew and the egbere marks the new owner as the new thief. If the egbere is somehow prevented from returning to the proximity of its mat or the one who stole it (perhaps the thief travels to another plane) then the mat stops working after a week. If the egbere dies, its mat loses all magical powers.

Locate Thief (Su)

If an egbere’s mat is stolen, it knows where both the thief and its mat are at all times (as if using discern location).

Nightbound (Su)

An egbere returns to the First World when the sun rises and reappears at sunset.

Relentless Jaunt (Su)

As a swift action, the egbere teleports (as if using greater teleport) to appear 60 feet away from the thief (or as close to 60 feet as it can get).

Sorrowful Wailing (Su)

An egbere’s cries drain hope, motivation, and joy from those who steal from them. When a creature who has stolen an egbere’s mat is within 60 feet of the egbere, that creature must roll two d20s whenever it makes a d20 roll (such as an attack roll, skill check, or saving throw) and must use the lower result. When making attack rolls against the thief, other creatures roll two d20s and take the higher result. While under this effect the thief cannot benefit from competence, luck, and morale bonuses. The thief doesn’t have to see or hear the egbere to be affected by this ability. All other creatures may find this wailing unsettling but are otherwise unaffected by it.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate plains and forests
Organization solitary
Treasure Egbere mat

GM Note

Be aware, while 1 gp doubling each week might not seem like a lot, a thief who can endure for 21 weeks would possess over 1 million gold pieces. It is a good idea to consider how this episode of avarice, wealth and greed will conclude for your PCs.

Alternatively, there are egberes who are less malevolent and more enigmatic in nature (true neutral instead of neutral evil). If a character knowingly tracks down such an egbere, takes its mat, and tolerates the egbere’s haunting wail for a set period of time, usually a week or even up to a month, then the egbere provides a gift of wealth for this grueling feat of resilience. From a gamist point of view this allows a PC the option to play on ‘hard mode’ for a period in return for a levelappropriate monetary reward at the end.

Egbere, also known as bush babies, are childlike, melancholy Fey that inhabit the farthest flung places in the bush. They were once greedy and selfish humans, but the gods punished them by transforming them into these pitiful creatures.

Egbere wander the wilderness at night, wailing because of their lot in life. They have one possession, a woven straw mat, and they cannot acquire more no matter how much they try.

If a non-Fey creature steals an egbere’s mat, they become rich, but most people who live in parts inhabited by egbere know better; while not physically dangerous, egbere haunt thieves until they give the mat back. Their haunting is so unpleasant that most rapidly return the stolen mat.

An egbere makes no effort to defend itself or to harm would-be thieves. Its incessant crying is a far worse punishment to thieves than any harm it might physically inflict. Egbere cease to exist when the sun rises and come back into existence when the sun sets.

Legends tell of people who have stolen mats from numerous egbere, and now a horde of the wailing childlike Fey follow them around as they gain riches. Rich, they may grow, but the lives of such thieves are indescribably awful, due to the incessant cries of so many egbere.
